name: The Lich's Muzzle
object: A bit-and-collar of grey iron on a cracked leather strap, its inner face scored with a ring of tiny script. It hung beside a workbench in Vynan, the dead laboratory of the lich Ivextus of Gral, and the grooves in the bit are not from tools.
unlock: Find a spellcaster who wore a muzzle like it, and learn what the lich kept them from saying
Wear it yourself through one whole conversation without speaking a word
risk: The collar fights its wearer. Make a WIL save, DC 13, when the conversation ends. On a failure it stays fastened until someone says your name over it, and you are Silenced until then.

resource.name: Hush
resource.text: Hush (toggle, on/off). Hush is on while the muzzle's circle holds and off when you remove the muzzle (an Action) or drop to 0 HP. It does not turn off at a rest. A fastened muzzle clears only when you carry it to a spellcaster who speaks your name over it. While Hush is on you are Silenced too.

powers: Hush (Action, turn Hush on): Everything within 2 spaces of you goes quiet. Each creature in that circle, you included, is Silenced while it stays there. At the start of its turn a creature may make a WIL save, DC 13; on a success it speaks and casts freely that turn. Solo creatures save with advantage.
Last Word (Free, 1/encounter, while Hush is on): When a creature in the circle tries to cast a spell and cannot, you hear the first word of it. The GM tells you the spell's name and school.
escalation: If Hush stays on through a Safe Rest, the muzzle fastens: you cannot take it off, and you cannot speak, until a spellcaster speaks your name over it. The Mages of Kartan sense a Silenced hero in the city and send someone with a key to the strap within a session.
cracker: Learn the last word Ivextus kept inside the muzzle, and speak it in Vynan. Hush now covers only the creatures you choose, and you are no longer Silenced by it. Kartan wants the word, and sends someone to ask.
notes: Fold 4. Fills the Silenced gap and the counter-caster role. [TABLE ROLL: who else wore muzzles in Vynan.]

matrix.refill: Carry a fastened muzzle to a spellcaster who speaks your name
matrix.cost: you are Silenced too; fastening; Kartan sends someone

name: The Iverundian Calipers
object: A pair of brass calipers longer than a forearm, their legs marked in a scale no city measure uses. They were cut in Io, the forge-world of the fallen god Iverundus, to check colossal war-machines against his standard, and the Iverundians still list one gauge of the set as missing.
unlock: Measure a creature no one has recorded, and give the reading to the Library of Vrassa or the Seekers of the Sun
Take the measure of a hostile creature at arm's length, with the Calipers closed on it, for a full round
risk: The creature does not stand still. It makes one free attack against you during the round, and you cannot Defend against it.

resource.name: Readings
resource.text: Readings (pip tracker, max 3). Regain 1 each time you give a reading of a kind of creature, machine or place that the Library of Vrassa, the Seekers of the Sun or an Iverundian does not yet hold, and they write it down. Readings return only this way.

powers: Take the Measure (Action, spend 1 Reading): Choose a creature within Reach 2 and close the Calipers on it. You Assess it, choosing any of the three Assess options, without a skill check, and this does not use up a skill for the encounter. It is also Weakened X until the end of its next turn, where X is your level.
Gauge (Free, when you Assess a creature): The GM also tells you its level, its armor type and its saves.
escalation: When you spend the last Reading, the jaws close on you: you are Weakened X (X is your level) on your next attack. An Iverundian is sent through the arch within a session to check the gauge against the standard, politely, and to ask where you found it.
cracker: Carry the Calipers to Io and set them against the god's own standard. They are recalibrated and cut a gauge of your own: Weakened X is your level plus the better of your STR or DEX, and Gauge works on any creature in sight. The Iverundians keep a record of every reading you take.
notes: Fold 4. Rises with level: Weakened X scales with monster damage. Uses Assess, which no other card touches.

matrix.refill: Give a reading of something unrecorded to the Library, the Seekers or an Iverundian
matrix.cost: a free attack at unlock; Weakened on you at 0; an Iverundian collector

name: The Dead-God's Vial
object: A stoppered vial of black glass, cold to hold, half full of thick ichor drawn from the petrified vein of a titan-god in Threska's Desert of Dead Gods. The council that served the Nameless King milked these gods for their experiments, and never finished with them.
unlock: Learn from a healer or a dead temple what the ichor does to a living body
Go a day in the desert without water, then give the vial a drop of your own blood
risk: The ichor tests you. Make a STR save, DC 14. On a failure you are Poisoned until someone heals you.

resource.name: Taint
resource.text: Taint (d6 vs. accumulation). Each time you Coat a weapon, roll a d6 against the Taint you had before, then add 1 Taint. If you roll equal to or below it, the ichor reaches you (see Escalation). Taint has no maximum, so at 6 or more every Coat reaches you. Taint clears only when you carry the vial back to a dead god's vein in Threska and pour a measure back.

powers: Coat (Action, +1 Taint): Coat a weapon or a handful of ammunition. The next creature you hit with it this encounter makes a STR save, DC 13, or is Poisoned until it is healed. Solo creatures save with advantage.
Bitter Blood (Passive): You cannot be Poisoned by anything except the vial.
escalation: When the ichor reaches you, you are Poisoned until someone heals you, and the vial hums for the dead god's heirs. Within a session the Knights of the Nameless King come asking who has been drawing on Threska's gods.
cracker: Pour the rest back into the vein and speak the god's name. It forgives you the debt: Taint stops climbing, and Coat ignores Solo advantage on the save. The Knights learn a god has been spoken to, and send a priest to ask what it said.
notes: Fold 4. Poisoned (disadvantage, healing ends it) counters healers and is flat across levels, as a monster's flat d20 save holds.

matrix.refill: Carry the vial back to a dead god's vein in Threska and pour a measure back
matrix.cost: Taint reaches you; Knights of the Nameless King

name: The Veles-Lamp
object: A squat lantern of black stone with a lens of red glass, carved by the people of Kor and lit from the star Veles that hangs over Korax. Its wick burns nothing, and the flame inside is the colour of dried blood.
unlock: Light the lamp at the skull-mouth cave that opens into the Red Deeps, under Veles, with one of the people of Kor looking on
Carry it lit through the Red Deeps until you reach the surface again
risk: Something in the Red Deeps follows the light. Make a Stealth check, DC 13, on the way out. On a failure it follows you through the arch within a session.

resource.name: Light
resource.text: Light (Wound-cost, paid in Hit Dice). Keeping the lamp bright costs Hit Dice, as each power says. Spent Hit Dice return only as Hit Dice normally do, on a Safe Rest, and the lamp never refills them.

powers: Brighten (Action, spend 1 Hit Die, no healing): A red light fills a 6-space radius around you until the end of the encounter, or for an hour outside one. Creatures in the light cannot hide, and Invisible creatures in it are seen. Allies in the light cannot be Frightened.
Dim (Free): Put the lamp out. The Hit Die is not returned.
escalation: If you have no Hit Die to spend, Brighten costs 1 Wound instead. Each time that happens, Veles notices: the people of Kor send a runner through the arch to ask who is spending their light.
cracker: Carry the flame back to the skull-mouth cave and let Veles see it burn. The lamp burns free: Brighten costs no Hit Die. The light draws the Red Deeps, and once per arc something that hunts by light comes for its owner.
notes: Fold 4. Fills light and dark, and the found-card Wound-cost gap. Hit Dice are on the sheet, so the cost can be tracked. The spec's Wound-cost type spends Wounds; this card pays Hit Dice first and Wounds only when out, a deliberate variant.

matrix.refill: None: the cost is paid in Hit Dice, which return on a Safe Rest
matrix.cost: Hit Dice; Wounds when out; the people of Kor

name: The Worldtree Whistle
object: A whistle carved from a splinter of the dead Worldtree of Eruwynd, pale and light as bone, with a hunter's notch cut for every beast it has called. It came off a dwarven airship hunter who did not come back from the Endless Forest.
unlock: Hunt beside a dwarven airship hunter of Eruwynd for a whole hunt, and share what you take
Blow the whistle alone at dusk at the foot of the dead Worldtree, and wait until something answers
risk: What answers tests you first. Make a Naturecraft check, DC 14. On a failure it fights you as a monster of your level, and the bond takes only if you win without killing it.

resource.name: Trust
resource.text: Trust (pip tracker, max 3). Spend 1 Trust each time you Call. Regain 1 each time you feed the companion from your own hand and hunt with it through a full day of downtime (the Mentor downtime, with the beast as your pupil). Trust returns only this way, and a companion with no Trust will not answer the whistle.

powers: Call (Action, spend 1 Trust): Your companion arrives within 12 spaces and stays for the encounter, or for an hour outside one. Build it from the Monster Builder at your level minus 4 (minimum 1/2): its HP from the Unarmored column, one attack from the 1-attack damage column, Speed 6, no armor, no crits. You move it and roll for it on your turn, after your own actions. It cannot Defend or Interpose.
Heel (Free): Your companion moves to a space adjacent to you and makes no attack this round.
escalation: If your companion drops to 0 HP, it flees and Trust falls to 0. It will not answer until you have spent a day finding it and caring for it. The hunters of Eruwynd hear the whistle was blown, and send one to ask what you have done with their beast.
cracker: Take the companion back to the dead Worldtree and let it choose. If it stays, it follows your level minus 2, not 4, and Heel costs it nothing. If it goes, it leads its herd to your call once per arc: three companions at your level minus 6. Either way a hunter of Eruwynd comes to see what the whistle called.
notes: Fold 4. Rises with level (Monster Builder). The player runs the companion, which settles the table question. Level minus 4 keeps it near half a hero. At minus 2 it was a full extra hero: a 100 HP, 30 damage ally at level 10.

matrix.refill: Feed the companion by hand and hunt with it through a full day of downtime
matrix.cost: Trust; the companion can flee; hunters of Eruwynd
matrix.look: pale whistle of dead Worldtree wood

name: The Silent Partner's Chop
object: A jade seal the size of a thumb, its face a tangle of characters no clerk in Market Square can read. It is stamped at the foot of contracts in a dozen stalls, and the merchants who hold those contracts will not say who they answer to.
unlock: Seal a contract with a merchant of Market Square who will not say who they answer to
Put in a sum you cannot afford to lose: every coin you carry
risk: The partner audits you. Make an Insight check, DC 14, to read who the merchant answers to. On a failure the Black Hand learns you hold a stamp and sends a collector within a session.

resource.name: Stakes
resource.text: Stakes (pip tracker, max 3). Spend 1 Stake per Bought Time. Regain 1 each time you put gold into a business or trade venture in the city (the Invest downtime), worth at least 25 gp per level, and bring the receipt back to the Chop's partner: a clerk, a stall, a name you are given. Stakes return only this way.

powers: Bought Time (Action, spend 1 Stake): Name a fine, bribe or debt of up to 50 gp times your level. The partner pays it directly, so you never hold the gold, and writes it down. You owe them a favour of the same worth: the GM presents it as a job in your next episode.

Silent Partner (Passive, when you miss an episode): The Chop closes a deal while you are away. At the start of your next episode the GM gives you one true, incomplete rumour about a person, place or faction in the city.
escalation: When the last Stake is spent, the partner calls in the books. Within a session a clerk from a stall you invested in comes asking for the favour you owe, and the Black Hand wants its tax. If you cannot pay, the Chop goes cold until you do.
cracker: The partner comes due, in person. Sit across from them in the stalls and take the trade they offer. Take over the partnership, so Bought Time owes no favour and the Black Hand taxes you in earnest. Or sell your share for double everything you invested, and the Chop goes dark for good.
notes: Fold 4. The only card that does something when its owner is absent, and the only Invest refill. A gold sink that scales with level.

matrix.refill: Invest gold in a city business and bring the receipt to the partner
matrix.cost: gold; a favour owed; the Black Hand's tax

name: The Standing Invitation
object: A stiff cream card edged in gold leaf, lettered in the court hand of the Golden Order and addressed to the bearer, and one. No host's name is printed on it, and the clerks of the Golden Council insist the Order never issued it.
unlock: Present the card at the door of a gathering held by a house of the Golden Order, and be admitted without anyone asking whose guest you are
Stay until the last guest has left, and tell no one who asks how you were invited
risk: Someone there knows the card. Make a Stealth check, DC 13, to leave unfollowed. On a failure a Golden Council clerk starts a six-step clock about who issued it.

resource.name: Seat
resource.text: Seat (session-bound ritual). Spend the Seat each time you Take a Seat. The Seat clears at a Safe Rest only if, since you last spent it, you have hosted or attended a gathering of at least three guests who did not arrive with you (the Socialize downtime), and brought a gift to the host. If you skipped it, the Safe Rest does not clear the Seat.

powers: Take a Seat (Action, spend the Seat): Enter a gathering held by any faction of the city: a feast, a trial, a council, a wake. You are admitted and seated as an invited guest. The host cannot have you removed without first asking you to leave, in front of the guests.
Name on the Card (Passive): At each Safe Rest the card shows a house and an hour. The GM chooses the gathering when you arrive, and you may offer it to the table as a door.
escalation: If you use the Seat on a gathering the card was not meant for, the true host shows themself. The GM names a house of the Golden Order, and it wants to know why a stranger holds its card. The Seat stays spent until you attend a gathering that house hosts.
cracker: Host a gathering of your own with the card as the invitation, and let the guests learn who sent it. The houses owe you a seat: the Seat clears at any Safe Rest after you attend any gathering. One house of the Golden Order is your enemy for it.
notes: Fold 4. Access without a persuasion override. Uses the session-bound ritual type, which no card uses. [TABLE ROLL: which house issued it.]

matrix.refill: Host or attend a gathering of three or more strangers and bring the host a gift
matrix.cost: the Seat stays spent; a Golden Council clock

name: The Deathreach Chalk
object: A stub of white chalk the length of a finger, worn to the shape of a hand, taken from the living dungeon of Deathreach. Lines drawn with it in the Dead Fingers have never faded, and the walls near them have grown.
unlock: Draw a door in a wall of the Dead Fingers, and walk through it
Leave something of your own in the room beyond, to be found
risk: Deathreach notices the line. Make a DEX save, DC 13, as the passage closes behind you. On a failure you take 2d6 bludgeoning and are sealed in until someone cuts you out with a Might check, DC 14.

resource.name: Chalk
resource.text: Chalk (pip tracker, max 3). Spend 1 Chalk per Draw a Door or Seal. Regain 1 each time you spend a day of downtime on a Build: draw a plain stone room onto a holding or guild hall, which fills no upgrade slot, and let Deathreach grow it. Chalk returns only this way, and each room ticks a Deathreach clock (start one if there is none).

powers: Draw a Door (Action, spend 1 Chalk): Draw a doorway on a stone or earth wall, floor or ceiling you can reach. It opens a passage up to 2 spaces wide, 2 high and 2 deep until the end of the encounter or an hour, then the stone closes and expels anything inside to the nearest open space. It cannot cross an arch or magic-worked stone.
Seal (Action, spend 1 Chalk): Draw a line across a door or passage. For an hour it holds like a wall: a creature must pass a Might check, DC 14, to break through.
Mark (Free): Draw a sign on a surface you touch. You know when any creature crosses it, for an hour.
escalation: When the last Chalk is spent, the stub is too short to hold a line: the next door you draw does not close. It stays open, a hole between two places, and creatures of the dungeon come through it within a session.
cracker: Draw one door and let it stay: a permanent passage, 2 spaces wide, between your holding and one place in the city, never an arch. Every faction that wants a route knows where it is.
notes: Fold 4. FLAGGED: private doors cut against 'keys are power'. The cap (2 spaces, no arch, city only at Cracker) is a proposal for the GM to rule on.

matrix.refill: Build: draw a room onto a holding or guild hall (downtime day)
matrix.cost: sealed in on a failed unlock; an open hole at 0; a Deathreach clock
